units.passage: It is important that faculty clearly communicate to students the acceptable use of generative AI in their course(s).
units.policy: Faculty clearly communicate to students the acceptable use of generative AI in their course(s).
units.why: "It is important that faculty clearly communicate to students the acceptable use of generative AI" tells instructors to state their expectations; P09 fits (state AI expectations to students).

units.passage: Such communication should be included via a statement in the syllabus and/or Canvas course site in addition to verbally communicating the faculty’s position in class
units.policy: The AI expectations statement should be included in the syllabus and/or the Canvas course site.
units.why: Says communication 'should be included via a statement in the syllabus and/or Canvas course site', which directs where the AI statement goes: P09.

units.passage: Instructors are encouraged to reiterate course expectations around the use or prohibition of generative AI tools
units.why: 'Instructors are encouraged to reiterate course expectations around the use or prohibition of generative AI tools' asks instructors to restate rules at course level; P09 is the nearest type though this is a restating, hence the fit note.
units.fit_note: It restates existing course rules rather than asking for a first syllabus statement.

units.passage: the Office of Academic Integrity encourages instructors to set clear expectations around proper usage in their syllabus and on assignment rubrics.
units.policy: The Office of Academic Integrity encourages instructors to set clear expectations around proper usage in their syllabus and on assignment rubrics.
units.why: The Office "encourages instructors to set clear expectations around proper usage in their syllabus and on assignment rubrics"; this asks for syllabus and rubric statements, so P09.

units.passage: As Generative AI tools like ChatGPT become more accessible, instructors are encouraged to set clear expectations around proper usage.
units.why: 'instructors are encouraged to set clear expectations around proper usage' is a request to state AI rules at course level: P09, instructor, should.

units.passage: The Office of Academic Integrity encourages instructors to outline expectations in their course syllabus and identify if (and to what extent) using Generative AI is appropriate.
units.why: The Office asks instructors to 'outline expectations in their course syllabus and identify if (and to what extent) using Generative AI is appropriate': a syllabus AI statement, P09, should.

units.passage: Whatever any given individual instructor decides should be clearly communicated to students in course materials.
units.why: 'Whatever any given individual instructor decides should be clearly communicated to students in course materials': an AI statement in course materials, P09.

units.passage: if you wish to discourage student use of generative AI, let your students know this expectation both in your syllabus and in class.
units.why: 'if you wish to discourage student use of generative AI, let your students know this expectation both in your syllabus and in class' tells instructors to communicate a discouraging rule: P09.
units.fit_note: The option is to discourage AI (P03), not ban it.

units.passage: Include GAI expectations and policies on each course syllabus
units.why: Headline guideline to put GAI policy on every syllabus: 'Include GAI expectations and policies on each course syllabus'. It is an imperative applied to 'each course', under guidelines that 'articulate expectations', and the page later repeats it as a duty ('Instructors are responsible for communicating their policies'), so modality must; P09 matches exactly.
units.fit_note: Heading phrased as an expectation; the modal is implied rather than stated

units.passage: Address issues such as: the types of resources students can use for which assignments; how and when GAI platforms may be used; how and when students can work together on assignments; appropriate citation methods, etc.
units.policy: The syllabus statement addresses the types of resources students can use for which assignments, how and when GAI platforms may be used, how and when students can work together, and appropriate citation methods.
units.why: Lists what a syllabus statement should cover: 'the types of resources students can use for which assignments; how and when GAI platforms may be used'. It is the content spec of the P09 syllabus requirement, not a separate rule about what is allowed.

units.passage: Syllabus statements provide clarity for all students and support their success.
units.why: Gives the reason for syllabus statements: they 'provide clarity for all students and support their success'. Nearest type is P09 since it justifies the syllabus requirement.
units.fit_note: Rationale for the syllabus requirement rather than the requirement itself. | Coder B (P66): Gives a reason for stating rules, not for the rules themselves

units.passage: The absence of GAI guidance in a course undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate instances of academic misconduct.
units.policy: The absence of GAI guidance in a course undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate instances of academic misconduct.
units.why: Argues why silence is a problem: 'absence of GAI guidance ... undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate' misconduct. It supports the syllabus requirement (P09); it gives no fallback rule so P06 does not fit.
units.fit_note: Rationale: missing guidance undermines adjudication; no default rule stated. | A reason for the syllabus requirement and a link to enforceability, not the requirement itself

units.passage: Instructors are responsible for communicating their policies and guidelines to students.
units.why: 'Instructors are responsible for communicating their policies and guidelines to students' puts the duty to communicate AI expectations on instructors; P09 fits.

units.passage: In order to substantiate cases of academic misconduct, instructional materials (such as the course syllabus, assignment prompts, and/or verbal instructions) need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or citing such use; in short, when and how GAI tools can be used, along with when and how such use should be acknowledged.
units.policy: Instructional materials such as the course syllabus, assignment prompts, and verbal instructions need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or citing such use.
units.why: Says materials 'need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or citing', a requirement to state expectations (P09) in syllabus, prompts or verbally.
units.fit_note: Also requires naming the disclosure or citation method, and ties it to enforceability

units.passage: Academic integrity and learning: Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology, its role, if any, in their learning and skills development, and they need clear communication about the consequences of inappropriate use of GAI technologies.
units.policy: Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology and its role, if any, in their learning and skills development.
units.why: 'Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology' restates the clear-expectations requirement (P09) as a program discussion topic.
units.fit_note: Also asks for clear communication of consequences, which is partly P123

units.passage: This decision comes with the obligation to accurately and clearly communicate AI policies to students enrolled in WSU courses across all campuses.
units.why: "This decision comes with the obligation to accurately and clearly communicate AI policies to students" binds instructors to communicate their rule across all campuses; P09 is the nearest type, though this sentence is the general duty rather than the syllabus requirement.
units.fit_note: Names a duty to communicate AI policy to students on all campuses, without naming the syllabus. | General duty to communicate AI policy accurately and clearly to students on all campuses; not specifically the syllabus statement.

units.passage: The Office of the Provost expects every instructor to set clear expectations and policies related to acceptable AI use in their course(s).
units.why: "The Office of the Provost expects every instructor to set clear expectations and policies related to acceptable AI use" states a university expectation that instructors set AI rules before the course; "expects" is coded should (as with "expected to"), P09 (an AI policy for every course). Only coder A found it.

units.passage: Instructors must clearly indicate their course policy about AI use in every class syllabus, and potentially, for each and every assessment.
units.why: "Instructors must clearly indicate their course policy about AI use in every class syllabus" is a must-rule requiring an AI statement in each syllabus, the definition of P09.

units.passage: Instructors must clearly indicate their course policy about AI use in every class syllabus, and potentially, for each and every assessment.
units.policy: Instructors potentially state their AI policy for each and every assessment as well as in the syllabus.
units.why: "and potentially, for each and every assessment" extends the syllabus duty to individual assessments, but only "potentially", so the instructor may state the AI policy per assessment; P09 (AI statement), instructor, course-start, may.

units.passage: If you decide to allow generative AI as a tool for learning in your courses, clarify for your students the circumstances in which AI is allowable.
units.why: Step 1 says that if you allow AI "clarify for your students the circumstances in which AI is allowable"; it tells instructors to state allowed uses, which is communication (P09).
units.fit_note: Applies to instructors who allow AI: say in which circumstances it is allowed.

units.passage: As a reminder, any expectations about AI usage should be communicated in writing to students.
units.why: "any expectations about AI usage should be communicated in writing to students" adds a writing requirement to communication, P09.
units.fit_note: Specifies that AI expectations be communicated in writing, not only orally.

units.passage: Because the WAC doesn’t explicitly mention AI, and given the rapid evolution of AI and conflicting policies among instructors, we recommend that each instructor develop a clear and explicit policy regarding the (un)acceptable use of AI in their class.
units.why: The page tells instructors to "develop a clear and explicit policy regarding the (un)acceptable use of AI in their class"; a policy-statement duty, P09.

units.passage: We recommend that instructors avoid relying on the WAC to do the work of communicating their AI policy.
units.why: "We recommend that instructors avoid relying on the WAC to do the work of communicating their AI policy" is advice on how to communicate; P09.
units.fit_note: Says not to rely on the general academic-integrity code in place of an AI statement.

units.passage: We also recommend reiterating the policy often in a variety of ways and consider including the policy in assignment or verbal instructions in addition to the syllabus statement.
units.why: "reiterating the policy often in a variety of ways" and including it in assignment instructions asks for repeated communication beyond the syllabus, nearest P09.
units.fit_note: Adds repetition and placement in assignment or verbal instructions, not just a syllabus statement. | Repeat the policy often and in assignment or verbal instructions, beyond the syllabus.

units.passage: Instructors are responsible for communicating academic integrity expectations, which may now include information about using Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools like ChatGPT in your coursework.
units.why: "Instructors are responsible for communicating academic integrity expectations, which may now include information about using Artificial Intelligence"; duty to state AI expectations, P09.

units.passage: Faculty need to clearly communicate their expectations to their students about how AI should or should not be used. This can be done with syllabus language and policies; general classroom discussions; demonstrations with AI to illustrate its use, shortcomings, output analysis, biases; guidelines on assignments.
units.why: The report says "faculty need to clearly communicate their expectations to their students about how AI should or should not be used", a duty to state AI expectations (P09).

units.passage: The syllabus needs to include an explanation of the ways in which AI may be used in a class and why (not).
units.why: The report says "the syllabus needs to include an explanation of the ways in which AI may be used in a class and why (not)", a syllabus duty (P09); the "why" part is P66 but the duty to state expectations is primary.
units.fit_note: Also asks that the reasons be given.

units.passage: We also feel that providing guidance in the syllabus is essential and suggest that perhaps the syllabus template include a header where an instructor may state, explicitly, their policy on AI for their course(s).
units.why: The committee suggests "the syllabus template include a header where an instructor may state, explicitly, their policy on AI", a syllabus template duty (P09).

units.passage: Some instructors may prefer to explicitly state the university policy on academic misconduct in their syllabi to draw student attention to it.
units.why: 'Some instructors may prefer to explicitly state the university policy on academic misconduct in their syllabi' is an optional restatement of the misconduct policy (P09).
units.fit_note: Optional restatement of the misconduct policy in syllabi.

units.passage: • Consider the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in your course. o Include a syllabus statement on the use of AI ▪ Will you allow students to use AI to help them with assignments? Within what parameters? ▪ Will you use AI as a teaching tool to show students the limitations of its use, benefits, and drawbacks? ▪ Will you ban the use of all AI in your class? 10
units.why: 'Include a syllabus statement on the use of AI' asks every instructor to state a position (P09).

units.passage: Provide a statement as to the expectations for how AI should or should not be used in the composition of the essay.
units.why: For undergraduate admissions the report asks to "provide a statement as to the expectations for how AI should or should not be used in the composition of the essay", stating expectations (P09).
units.fit_note: Applies to admission essays, not syllabi. An expectations statement in the admissions application, not a syllabus.

units.passage: As part of the application for admission where students must submit an essay, either: • Provide a statement as to the expectations for how AI should or should not be used in the application process.
units.why: For graduate admissions the report asks to "provide a statement as to the expectations for how AI should or should not be used in the application process", stating expectations (P09).
units.fit_note: Applies to graduate admission applicants. Graduate application, not a syllabus.

units.passage: Advisors agreed that the syllabus should be where instructors provide students their guidelines on using AI for coursework.
units.why: Advisors "agreed that the syllabus should be where instructors provide students their guidelines on using AI for coursework", locating the AI rule in the syllabus (P09).

units.passage: To support student compliance with the Honor Code, all instructors are urged to include an explicit AI policy in every course syllabus, discuss academic integrity at the start of their class, and have their students sign the Honor Pledge on all assignments and tests.
units.why: Instructors are 'urged to include an explicit AI policy in every course syllabus': a recommendation, so should; actor instructor; phase before-course (policy design). P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus) fits, though it is urged rather than required.
units.fit_note: Worded as 'urged', not a mandate as P09 usually implies.

units.passage: This means that students need clarity on the use of Generative AI in each of their different courses
units.why: "students need clarity on the use of Generative AI in each of their different courses" justifies per-course statements; nearest is P09, but it is a rationale for them, hence the fit note.
units.fit_note: States the need for course-level clarity as a reason, not a duty to include a statement.

units.passage: we encourage faculty to share their expectations on the use of GenAI with their students in each course syllabus.
units.why: 'we encourage faculty to share their expectations on the use of GenAI with their students in each course syllabus' recommends syllabus AI expectations: P09, instructor, before-course, should.

units.passage: If you encourage experimentation with AI, detail how and what uses of AI tools are appropriate.
units.why: 'If you encourage experimentation with AI, detail how and what uses of AI tools are appropriate' asks instructors who permit AI to spell out permitted uses; nearest is P09 (state AI expectations), instructor, should.
units.fit_note: Specifically about detailing appropriate uses where AI is encouraged.

units.passage: To support student compliance with the Honor Code, all instructors are urged to include an explicit AI policy in every course syllabus, discuss academic integrity at the start of their class, and have their students sign the Honor Pledge on all assignments and tests.
units.why: Instructors are 'urged to include an explicit AI policy in every course syllabus': a recommendation, so should; actor instructor; phase before-course (policy design). P09 (state AI expectations in the syllabus) fits, though it is urged rather than required.
units.fit_note: Worded as 'urged', not a mandate as P09 usually implies.

units.passage: This means that students need clarity on the use of Generative AI in each of their different courses.
units.why: 'students need clarity on the use of Generative AI in each of their different courses' is the stated reason for asking instructors to put expectations in each syllabus. It is a principle (general, informs) and is closest to P09 (syllabus statement), as a reason for it and not a duty.
units.fit_note: A: A rationale for clear per-course communication rather than a duty to discuss the rules. B: States the need for course-level clarity as a reason, not a duty to include a statement.

units.passage: we encourage faculty to share their expectations on the use of GenAI with their students in each course syllabus.
units.why: 'we encourage faculty to share their expectations on the use of GenAI with their students in each course syllabus' recommends syllabus AI expectations: P09, instructor, before-course, should.

units.passage: If you encourage experimentation with AI, detail how and what uses of AI tools are appropriate.
units.why: 'If you encourage experimentation with AI, detail how and what uses of AI tools are appropriate' asks instructors who permit AI to specify uses; nearest is P09, instructor, should.
units.fit_note: Specifically about detailing appropriate uses where AI is encouraged.

units.passage: For example, faculty should be transparent about their expectations for AI use in the classroom to prevent students from getting into academic trouble if they use AI inappropriately.
units.why: Those in authority "should be transparent about their expectations for AI use in the classroom" so students avoid trouble; this asks faculty to state expectations, P09.
units.fit_note: Recommends transparency about expectations without strictly requiring a syllabus statement. Says to be transparent about expectations but does not say here that the statement must be in the syllabus.

units.passage: Transparency of the justification for AI use in a course. A clear, easy to understand syllabus statement on if and/or when students may use AI in their coursework.
units.why: Faculty teaching transparency: "A clear, easy to understand syllabus statement on if and/or when students may use AI" is a syllabus requirement of sorts, P09.

units.passage: Those rules are communicated frequently and clearly.
units.why: "Those rules are communicated frequently and clearly" describes repeated communication of classroom rules; nearest P09 (state expectations), but it is about frequency.
units.fit_note: Stresses communicating the rules frequently, beyond a one-time syllabus statement.

units.passage: The instructor will clearly state when and how it is permissible for students to use these tools
units.why: "The instructor will clearly state when and how it is permissible" commits the instructor to stating the AI rules (P09).
units.fit_note: Binds the instructor in the sample statement to state when and how; it is not a rule that every syllabus must carry a statement.

units.passage: RECOMMENDATION The Academic and Informational Technology Council and the Professional Concerns Committee recommend the required inclusion of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Statement on all WMU syllabi.
units.why: The recommendation says the committees 'recommend the required inclusion of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Statement on all WMU syllabi', a syllabus-statement requirement, P09.

units.passage: Thus, instructors should explicitly outline whether, and in what ways, AI tools may be used in their course.
units.why: It states 'instructors should explicitly outline whether, and in what ways, AI tools may be used in their course', a duty to state expectations, P09.

units.passage: Statement regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools (e.g., ChatGPT). The syllabus must make the expectations about AI use in the course explicit
units.why: The policy text adds a required element: 'Statement regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools (e.g., ChatGPT). The syllabus must make the expectations about AI use in the course explicit', P09.

units.passage: In the opinion of ATUS, the instructor needs to state when generative AI tools can or should not be used. A best practice would be to clearly outline AI policies, alongside plagiarism policies, within your course syllabus as well as on relevant assignments.
units.why: ATUS says the instructor 'needs to state when generative AI tools can or should not be used' and best practice puts AI policy in the syllabus and on assignments: a syllabus statement (P09).

units.passage: A best practice would be to clearly outline AI policies, alongside plagiarism policies, within your course syllabus as well as on relevant assignments.
units.why: "A best practice would be to clearly outline AI policies, alongside plagiarism policies, within your course syllabus" recommends a syllabus statement plus assignment-level notice, P09.

units.passage: If the instructor has allowed student use of AI, the allowed use should be made explicit within the assignment and/or syllabus, including the extent, methods, citations, and appropriateness of use.
units.why: "the allowed use should be made explicit ... including the extent, methods, citations, and appropriateness of use" says what an allowing instructor must spell out, still P09.

units.passage: Instructors who allow the use of generative AI in their classes incorporate protocols into their course syllabi and/or course content, and expressly communicate how this technology may be used.
units.why: Instructors who allow AI must 'incorporate protocols into their course syllabi and/or course content' and 'expressly communicate how this technology may be used', a syllabus-statement duty (P09). It binds only instructors who allow AI, which the fit note records.
units.fit_note: The duty applies only to instructors who allow AI; instructors who ban it are not required to state it, because the default already bans.

units.passage: Faculty members are expected to provide clear instructions on the permitted use of generative AI tools for academic work and requirements for attribution.
units.why: "Faculty members are expected to provide clear instructions on the permitted use of generative AI tools for academic work and requirements for attribution" obliges instructors to state AI rules in course materials: P09.

units.passage: These standards are set by instructors to support authentic learning and are detailed in the course syllabus or in the instructions for each course assignment.
units.why: "detailed in the course syllabus or in the instructions for each course assignment" says where instructor-set standards are written. P09 (rules stated in syllabus or assignment) fits; P78 not chosen because it is a duty on students to look it up.

units.passage: Your professor will state the level on the syllabus and on each assignment.
units.why: "Your professor will state the level on the syllabus and on each assignment" requires instructors to state AI expectations, P09.

units.passage: Instructors have a responsibility to set a clear AI policy and to communicate it; students have a responsibility to read it, understand it, and follow it.
units.why: "Instructors have a responsibility to set a clear AI policy and to communicate it" requires instructors to state a policy (P09).

units.passage: The course-level AI policy belongs on the syllabus.
units.why: "The course-level AI policy belongs on the syllabus" requires AI expectations in the syllabus (P09).

units.passage: The assignment-level policy belongs on the assignment itself, in a clearly marked section or box that states the applicable level, any assignment-specific conditions, and the consequences of noncompliance (see Appendix B).
units.why: "The assignment-level policy belongs on the assignment itself" and must state the level, conditions and "the consequences of noncompliance", so an assignment-level statement is required (P09).

units.passage: Faculty should make clear the expectations for academic integrity for their course.
units.why: "Faculty should make clear the expectations for academic integrity for their course" asks faculty to state expectations in the syllabus (P09).

units.passage: Always give an explicit list of allowed electronic platforms for each assignment. Include a statement in your syllabus about what is allowed or prohibited in the course.
units.why: "Always give an explicit list of allowed electronic platforms for each assignment" asks instructors to state allowed tools per assignment (P09).

units.passage: Include a statement in your syllabus about what is allowed or prohibited in the course.
units.why: "Include a statement in your syllabus about what is allowed or prohibited in the course" asks for a syllabus statement, P09.
